title: Clarity Engine — Config
description: Every tunable value in the clarity chain, pulled out of clarity-engine.js so it can be edited without touching code. Passed as { config } to `new ClarityEngine({ config })`. Any field left out falls back to clarity-config.default.json's value for that field.

gate.description: Background noise suppression. Implemented as a DynamicsCompressorNode pushed to a hard knee and steep ratio -- Web Audio has no native gate node, this is the real, standard approximation (see clarity-engine.js's own comment on this).

thresholdDb.description: Sound below this level gets suppressed. Lower (more negative) = only very quiet background gets cut. Higher (closer to 0) = more aggressive, risks cutting her quieter words too.

knee.description: 0 = hardest possible transition (truest gate behavior). Raise this if the gate feels too abrupt/choppy on her voice.

ratio.description: How hard the gate pushes down signal below threshold. 20 = near-total suppression. Lower it if it's cutting too much.

attackSec.description: How fast the gate closes when sound drops below threshold. Very fast by default so it doesn't clip the start of quiet background noise.

releaseSec.description: How fast the gate re-opens. Too fast and it 'pumps' audibly between her words; too slow and it's slow to suppress noise between sentences.

eq.description: Three-band EQ for speech intelligibility. This is the part most worth tuning per-person -- accents differ in which frequency bands carry the information you're missing.

lowShelf.description: Cuts rumble below speech range -- room hum, breath noise, distant traffic.

presence.description: The consonant-clarity band. This is the single most important knob for accent comprehension -- most of what makes an unfamiliar accent hard to parse is consonant onset/offset detail living in this range, not vowels.

frequencyHz.description: 2000-3000 generally covers consonant clarity. Try nudging toward 3000-3500 if 's'/'t'/'k' sounds specifically are what's getting lost.

q.description: How narrow the boosted band is. Lower = broader, gentler boost. Higher = more surgical, can sound harsh if pushed too far.

gainDb.description: How much to boost. Start conservative -- above ~8dB can start sounding harsh/sibilant.

highShelf.description: Slight lift to sibilance/air -- helps consonant edges (s, sh, t) read clearly without being harsh.

gain.description: Automatic makeup gain -- boosts her voice level overall.

db.description: Higher = louder overall. The limiter below prevents clipping even if this is pushed high, but very high values can amplify residual noise the gate didn't catch.

limiter.description: Final safety limiter -- catches any peaks the gain boost creates so nothing distorts, regardless of how high gain.db is set.

bufferSeconds.description: How far back you can rewind. Longer uses more memory (raw audio chunks held in the browser tab).

frameMs.description: Granularity of the rewind strip -- how finely you can jump to a specific moment. Smaller = finer control, more chunks to manage.

defaultReplaySpeed.description: Playback rate when replaying a buffered moment. Pitch is always preserved regardless of this value.

transcription.description: Optional live transcription backend. Leave endpoint null to disable this panel entirely.

endpoint.description: e.g. 'http://localhost:8420/transcribe' -- a local Whisper bridge. Null disables transcription; the audio clarity chain runs fully without it.

whisperModel.description: Not read by clarity-engine.js directly -- this documents which model the endpoint above should be running. 'medium' is the practical floor for accented speech; 'base' (many bridges' own default) is noticeably worse on non-American accents.
